**He went from touring in a cramped bus to winning an Oscar for pure comedy. Even Meryl Streep stood in awe.**

Born October 24, 1947, in St. Louis, Missouri, today Kevin Delaney Kline turns **79**, celebrated as the 'American Olivier' of stage and screen.

Originally studying classical piano and conducting at Indiana University, Kevin abandoned music for theater and spent four grueling years sleeping on buses in John Houseman's touring repertory troupe before Broadway noticed him.

Instead of chasing easy Hollywood paychecks after winning two early Tony Awards, he trusted an unorthodox instinct: blending high Shakespearean physical grace with fearless, manic slapstick comedy.

After a devastatingly raw film debut opposite Meryl Streep in *Sophie's Choice*, he unleashed unhinged comedic brilliance in *A Fish Called Wanda*, winning the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor—a rare triumph for a farce performance.

Behind the glamour, he fiercely protected his family life in Manhattan with wife Phoebe Cates, turning down blockbuster millions to stay rooted in live theater and raise their children away from tabloid chaos.

At 79, with an Oscar and three Tony Awards, Kevin Kline proves that true artistry knows no boundary between tragedy and laughter.

**What is the greatest Kevin Kline performance: A Fish Called Wanda, Dave, or In & Out? Drop your pick below! 👇**
posts.comment:

* Before switching to acting, Kevin studied classical piano and conducting at Indiana University, hoping to become a concert pianist.
* He is one of the very few actors in cinema history to win an Academy Award for a pure slapstick comedy performance as Otto West in *A Fish Called Wanda*.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: Before Hollywood crowned him an Oscar winner, Kevin Kline spent years living out of suitcases on a grueling repertory theater bus tour. He stunned critics opposite Meryl Streep in Sophie's Choice before stealing every scene in A Fish Called Wanda to capture Academy Award gold. Happy seventy-ninth birthday to a true giant of stage and screen. What is your favorite Kevin Kline movie of all time? Tell us in the comments.

**Cut from his teen TV show, he recorded mixtapes in a basement and conquered global music and television.**

Born October 24, 1986, in Toronto, Ontario, today Aubrey Drake Graham turns **40**, standing as a titan of modern entertainment and pop culture.

Raised by his single mother in the basement half of a rented Toronto house, young Aubrey supported his family with his modest acting paycheck playing Jimmy Brooks on *Degrassi: The Next Generation* until producers suddenly wrote off his character.

When record labels dismissed a former Canadian child actor trying to rap, Drake trusted an unorthodox instinct: blending vulnerable, melodic R&B singing directly into raw hip-hop confessionals.

His 2009 mixtape *So Far Gone* ignited a historic bidding war, launching an unprecedented run of Billboard number-one anthems while he returned to Hollywood as the powerhouse executive producer behind HBO's *Euphoria* and *Top Boy*.

Through relentless scrutiny, industry feuds, and the pressure of staying number one for fifteen straight years, he maintained a tireless studio work ethic that reshaped how the world streams music and television.

Entering his fourth decade at 40, Drake remains the ultimate blueprint for turning underdog ambition into a global empire.

**What is Drake's greatest era: Take Care, Nothing Was the Same, or Views? Share your pick below! 👇**

posts.caption:
**Dressed as a giant leaf in underwear ads, he quit everything and won the Best Actor Oscar in Amadeus.**

Born October 24, 1939, in Pittsburgh and raised in El Paso, Texas, today F. Murray Abraham turns **87**, revered as a towering master of dramatic acting.

The son of an Assyrian immigrant car mechanic, young Murray ran with a teenage street gang in Texas before a high school teacher placed Shakespeare in his hands, though by his late thirties he was stuck wearing a giant leaf costume in Fruit of the Loom underwear commercials.

Refusing to let his dream die as a punchline, he followed a bold instinct in 1978: he quit commercial work completely and became a stay-at-home dad while his wife worked as an office assistant to pay the rent.

That gamble paid off when he landed *Scarface* alongside Al Pacino and was cast as envious composer Antonio Salieri in Milos Forman's *Amadeus*, delivering a haunting performance that won the Academy Award for Best Actor.

Spending over four hours a day trapped in suffocating prosthetic aging makeup for *Amadeus*, he later conquered new generations in *Homeland*, *The Grand Budapest Hotel*, and *The White Lotus*.

At 87, F. Murray Abraham proves it is never too late to bet everything on your craft.

**Which F. Murray Abraham role is most unforgettable: Amadeus, Scarface, or The White Lotus? Comment below! 👇**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind F. Murray Abraham's stage name...**

* He added the initial 'F.' to his stage name Murray Abraham as a lifelong tribute to his father, Fahrid Abraham, an Assyrian immigrant who worked as an auto mechanic.
* Before winning his Oscar for *Amadeus*, he paid his bills for years playing the talking grape leaf in Fruit of the Loom commercials.

Which of these facts surprised you the most?
posts.reel_script: At thirty-nine years old, F. Murray Abraham was stuck wearing a giant grape leaf costume in television underwear commercials. He boldly quit his steady paycheck, stayed home raising his kids while chasing serious stage roles, and ultimately won the Best Actor Academy Award for his haunting portrayal of Salieri in Amadeus. Happy eighty-seventh birthday to an acting legend. What is your favorite F. Murray Abraham movie? Tell us below.

**He swept five major Broadway awards on his very first try. Then he brought dinosaurs to life for Spielberg.**

Born October 24, 1960, in San Francisco, California, today Bradley Darryl 'BD' Wong turns **66**, celebrated as one of Hollywood's most versatile character icons.

The son of a postal worker and telephone company supervisor, young Bradley faced an industry in the early 1980s that offered Asian-American actors almost nothing beyond stereotypes and one-line background bits.

When auditioning for Broadway's *M. Butterfly* in 1988, he trusted an unorthodox instinct: diving into rigorous Peking opera movement and psychological complexity that left producers breathless.

He became the only actor in Broadway history to win the Tony, Drama Desk, Outer Critics Circle, Clarence Derwent, and Theatre World awards for the same role, before Steven Spielberg cast him as geneticist Dr. Henry Wu in *Jurassic Park*.

Turning a brief two-minute lab scene in 1993 into the overarching villain of the billion-dollar *Jurassic World* trilogy—while voicing Captain Li Shang in *Mulan* and starring in *Law & Order: SVU* and *Mr. Robot*—he endured personal heartbreak after losing a premature twin son and authored a deeply moving memoir.

At 66, BD Wong stands as a fearless trailblazer across stage, film, and television.

**What is your favorite BD Wong role: Jurassic Park, Mulan, Law & Order: SVU, or Mr. Robot? Vote below! 👇**

🌟 FASCINATING FACTS & TRIVIA:
**The secret behind BD Wong's unmatched Broadway record...**

* For his 1988 Broadway debut in *M. Butterfly*, BD Wong became the only actor in history to sweep all five major New York theater awards for a single performance.
* Although Dr. Henry Wu was killed by raptors in Michael Crichton's original *Jurassic Park* novel, Steven Spielberg kept him alive on screen, allowing Wong to return twenty-two years later.

**Whenever James Bond was declared dead, Hollywood called one man. He saved 007 twice.**

Born October 24, 1943, in Hastings, New Zealand, today Martin Campbell turns **83**, honored as the undisputed master of practical action cinema.

Moving to London in 1966 with no industry connections, Martin started at the bottom lugging heavy camera rigs in British television studios and directing gritty, low-budget crime serials.

When the James Bond franchise stalled for six years after Cold War legal battles and critics called 007 an irrelevant relic, Martin trusted a bold instinct: stripping away cartoonish excess for bone-crunching stunts and emotional weight.

He launched Pierce Brosnan with the 1995 smash *GoldenEye*, revitalized swashbuckling cinema with Antonio Banderas in *The Mask of Zorro*, and then returned in 2006 to direct Daniel Craig in *Casino Royale*—widely hailed as the greatest Bond film ever made.

Refusing to rely on lazy green-screen CGI even in his seventies and eighties, he pushed stunt teams to flip real Aston Martins seven times and stage breathtaking crane jumps.

At 83, Martin Campbell remains the director who twice rescued cinema's longest-running spy empire.

**Thieves stole every dollar she had in Los Angeles. The day she packed to leave, one phone call changed her life.**

Born October 24, 1989, in Melbourne, Australia, today Eliza Jane Taylor turns **37**, beloved worldwide as a fearless television sci-fi heroine.

After spending her teens on the Australian soap *Neighbours*, Eliza moved to Los Angeles with her savings—only to have her credit card stolen and emptied at a hardware store after a month, leaving her broke and packing her bags to fly home in defeat.

Instead of boarding that flight, she followed a last-minute call from her manager: producers of a new sci-fi pilot had spotted an old audition tape of hers and wanted her to read the next morning.

Without even a formal cattle-call audition, she was cast as Clarke Griffin in *The 100*, leading seven intense seasons across 100 episodes as television's most complex post-apocalyptic commander before starring in *Quantum Leap*.

Filming grueling night shoots in freezing Vancouver forests while carrying the moral weight of a fiercely devoted global fanbase, she even found lifelong love by marrying her co-star Bob Morley.

At 37, Eliza Taylor's story is proof that breakthroughs arrive the second before you quit.

* Thieves stole her credit card in Los Angeles and spent all her remaining money at Home Depot the exact week before *The 100* producers called her in.
* She never did a formal open audition for Clarke Griffin; the showrunners discovered her from an old audition tape she had recorded months earlier for a movie.

After honing her craft at NYU Tisch and the Upright Citizens Brigade, Casey achieved her childhood dream by joining *Saturday Night Live* in 2008—only to be unceremoniously let go after two seasons.

Refusing to wait by the phone for bit parts, she trusted an unorthodox instinct: writing her own feature films with best friend June Diane Raphael and diving headfirst into fearless, rapid-fire ensemble comedy.

She co-wrote the box-office hit *Bride Wars*, became a cult television icon as Penny Hartz on ABC's *Happy Endings*, and stole scenes in David Fincher's Oscar-nominated thriller *Gone Girl* and Showtime's *Black Monday*.

Channeling the early grief of losing her mother Kathy into creating nonprofits and hilarious memoirs, she proved that vulnerability fuels the funniest art.

At 46, Casey Wilson is proof that getting fired from your dream job can launch your true legacy.
